'''Perkins:''' {{legend0|#ffb2b2|40–50%}} {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} {{legend0|#d72f30|70–80%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Ron Wyden]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Ron Wyden]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) | alliance2 = [[Constitution Party of Oregon|Constitution]] | alliance1 = [[Independent Party of Oregon|Independent Party]] | turnout = 66.91% {{decrease}} }} {{Elections in Oregon}} The '''2022 United States Senate election in Oregon''' was held on November 8, 2022, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Oregon]].{{Cite web|title=United States Senate election in Oregon, 2022|url=https://ballotpedia.org/United_States_Senate_election_in_Oregon,_2022|access-date=2020-09-11|website=Ballotpedia|language=en}} Incumbent [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] U.S. Senator [[Ron Wyden]], who was first elected in a [[1996 United States Senate special election in Oregon|1996 special election]], ran for a fifth full term.{{Cite news |last=Ligori |first=Crystal |date=January 2, 2021 |title=US Sen. Ron Wyden will seek reelection in 2022 |work=[[Oregon Public Broadcasting]] |url=https://www.opb.org/article/2021/01/01/us-senator-wyden-seeks-reelection-2022/ |url-status=live |access-date=March 2, 2021 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20210620033743/https://www.opb.org/article/2021/01/01/us-senator-wyden-seeks-reelection-2022/ |archive-date=June 20, 2021 }} [[Jo Rae Perkins]], who unsuccessfully ran for Oregon's other Senate seat in [[2020 United States Senate election in Oregon|2020]], won the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] primary with 33.3% of the vote.{{Cite news |date=2022-05-17 |title=Oregon Primary Election Results |language=en-US |work=The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2022/05/17/us/elections/results-oregon.html |access-date=2022-09-29 |issn=0362-4331}} The four candidates filing with the Oregon secretary of state for this election included Chris Henry of the [[Oregon Progressive Party]] and Dan Pulju of the [[Pacific Green Party]].{{Citation |title=Oregon SOS Candidate Filing Search |date=2022-10-12 |url=https://secure.sos.state.or.us/orestar/CFSearchPage.do}} Wyden ultimately won the election with 55.8% of the statewide vote. This was the first time since 1996 that none of the following counties went Democratic in a Senate Class III election: [[Gilliam County, Oregon|Gilliam]], [[Jackson County, Oregon|Jackson]], [[Marion County, Oregon|Marion]], [[Polk County, Oregon|Polk]], [[Wasco County, Oregon|Wasco]], and [[Yamhill County, Oregon|Yamhill]]. It was also the first time [[Columbia County, Oregon|Columbia County]] supported the Republican nominee in this seat since [[1986 United States Senate election in Oregon|1986]].{{Cite web |date=2022-11-08 |title=Wyden wins reelection, will return for 5th full Senate term |url=https://www.koin.com/news/elections/general-election-us-senate-seat-ron-wyden-jo-rae-perkins-11082022/ |access-date=2022-11-09 |website=KOIN.com |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221109225149/https://www.koin.com/news/elections/general-election-us-senate-seat-ron-wyden-jo-rae-perkins-11082022/ |archive-date=November 9, 2022 |url-status=dead}} == Democratic primary == === Candidates === ==== Nominee ==== *[[Ron Wyden]], incumbent U.S. senator (1996–present) ==== Eliminated in primary ==== * Will Barlow, former Electrical and Elevator Board member{{Cite web|title=BARLOW, WILLIAM EDWARD MR.
